hello.text: Beta! You finally remember where your mother lives. Have you eaten?

choices.text: Is there any work, Mummy? Anything you need?

worry.text: Hmph. You look thinner than at Navratri. Sit, sit. I'll make thepla.

food.text: Always dal-dhokli. Take a dabba home. And call your Pappa once in a while.

choices.text: Just visiting. Jai Shri Krishna, Mummy.

favor.text: Your Pappa's old Ambassador has to reach Rajesh Kaka's garage in the GIDC before he shuts. Pappa is at the derasar and you know he drives like a bullock cart. Can you take it? Don't scratch it.

choices.text: Of course. I'll take it right now.

yes.text: Keys are in the car outside. Rajesh Kaka closes soon, so go fast but carefully. And take this for petrol.

bye.text: Go, go. Come for dinner on Sunday, I'm making undhiyu.

k1.text: Bhai! Heard you're doing big things now. Airport, trains, all that. Kem cho?

k2.text: Chemical engineering exams. Again. Then a job in the GIDC, Pappa says. If you're flying out of Daman, tell Krupa at check-in I said hi.

k3.text: My lips are sealed. For a cutting chai at Hetal's, maybe.

s1.text: Kem cho! Cutting chai, extra adrak? Or are you here for the other business?

coffee.text: Here. Hot like the afternoon on the Vapi-Daman road.

dosa.text: Fresh khaman, with the green chutney you like.

work.text: Jignesh moves packages on the Western Railway locals for people who pay well. If you want in, find his marker at the station. He hates people who are late.
